claims.text: Adaptive neural-network potentials combined with nested sampling can substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed method can calculate free energies for both solid and fluid states of high-entropy systems.
Adaptive neural-network potentials can accurately capture vibrational entropy.
Adaptive neural-network potentials can accurately capture anharmonicity.
Adaptive neural-network potentials can accurately capture electron–vibration coupling.
Nested sampling efficiently explores the relevant free-energy landscape.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 2–5 relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 2–5 relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will improve accuracy by 10–20% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will improve accuracy by 10–20% relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method is applicable to high-entropy systems containing 3–6 principal elements.
The proposed method is applicable from 1000 K to 5000 K.
The accuracy of the adaptive neural-network potentials may depend on the specific high-entropy system.
The accuracy of the adaptive neural-network potentials may depend on training-data quality.
The efficiency of nested sampling may depend on the specific high-entropy system.
